guide_type: What kind of row this is. Empty or event — a performance, block — the start of a schedule block. All performances below it, up to the next block, belong to this block.
guide_number: The performance number. A whole number that must not repeat. It can be left empty — for a break, say.
guide_title: The performance title, or in a block row the block name, for example “Cosplay”.
guide_duration: The duration in seconds. A whole number: 900 is 15 minutes, 45 is a short act under a minute.
guide_nomination: The category, for example “Solo runway”. It can be left empty — breaks, the opening and the closing have no category.
guide_heading: What the file should look like
guide_intro: The schedule is read from the first sheet of the workbook. The first row holds the column headers, and below it there is one row for each performance and for the start of each block. Column names are written in Latin letters exactly as in the list below; the column order doesn't matter.
guide_required: All five columns are required, but the cells in type, number and nomination_title can be left empty. A performance row only needs title and duration, a block row needs type and title. Extra columns are ignored.
guide_replaces_title: The file fully replaces the schedule.
guide_replaces: Performances are matched by the number column: matching ones are updated, and those missing from the file are deleted. Rows without a number have nothing to match against, so they are added anew each time. Blocks are matched by title. The row order sets the order in the schedule.
